bearings.paper_claim: At 1000 nodes CELF++ with 50 MC sims per marginal estimate reached 122.95 +/- 24.37 vs IMM 954.90 +/- 1.27, i.e. 12.9 percent of IMM (t = -107.78, p < 0.001). Its CV rose to 71.5 percent at 500 nodes. The authors attribute the gap to MC budget and Python implementation but do not test that. The abstract gives 11.2 percent, which conflicts with the body.

bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's failure mode is independent noise across candidate estimates. CRN removes that for pairwise marginal comparison, so the CRN design is supported in principle. The paper uses undirected uniform-p IC; Melange runs competitive two-colour IC with seed gating on a 533-node kernel. The paper's numbers show the mechanism only.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers and CELF++ claims reproduced from the text. Analyst citations are wrong: the SEED keying is at lines 80-82 (not 66-69), and the MEA-7 ledger entry is at STATE.md 748-749 (not 765-768). The cross-seed pass predates QME fix 3 (comment at lines 80-81), so that leg used SEED-independent keys. The claim that the MC=100 leg stays valid is overstated: it was measured before fixes 1, 4, 5 and 7 changed the pools, draws and ranking, so it does not validate the current frontier. Re-measure under the current code before relying on it.

bearings.paper_claim: Theoretical guarantees such as the (1-1/e) bound can diverge sharply from realized performance when marginal gains are estimated by noisy simulation. CELF++ reached 12.9 percent of IMM at 1000 nodes.
bearings.paper_location: Abstract p.1 lines 13-16; Discussion p.13 lines 948-961
bearings.system_side: optimize.py runs a fixed-state lazy greedy over the INC grid (INC default 500 and BUDGET default 2500000 at line 26). Its docstring says the objective is separable and concave in a fixed stance state, and that highest-next-marginal selection is the exact discrete optimum. certificate_valid = fixed_state_concave and not conversions (lines 48 and 166); a modelled conversion switches the mode to modeled_threshold_replanning (line 190). No Monte Carlo call appears in the sections read.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's gap comes from MC estimation error, which does not arise in a deterministic objective, so the paper does not undercut the optimizer's fixed-state certificate. It would become relevant only if the objective were replaced by a simulated cascade.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claim checked against the text. System side checked by reading the docstring and certificate logic. The absence of Monte Carlo was read from excerpts, not from a full repo scan, so this is a partial check. The analyst's cites (3-10, 64-74, 156-163) are loose, but the content they point to matches.

bearings.paper_claim: Simple centrality seed rules come close to sampling-based IM under IC (PageRank 96.5 percent of IMM) at far lower runtime (2,304 vs 2.95 spread per second at 1000 nodes).
bearings.system_side: kb_benchmark.py computes Katz-Bonacich centrality on build_P(adj) at line 29, deterministically. It reports Spearman correlations of KB against four targets: the G-K allocation, observed CU money, observed industry money (banks plus finserv), and the legislative score (docstring lines 9-13; comparison list around lines 85-92). The brain records MEA-6 holistic KB-vs-allocation +0.225 at STATE.md lines 744-746, n=533. The benchmark does not score KB-top-k as a seed set under the cascade.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Adding a seed-spread column would test the paper's question on Melange's own kernel, as a diagnostic only, labelled UNSTRATIFIED, with window and denominator named. KB remains a model output, not a measure of access (D-025). Nothing in the chain consumes it.
bearings.verifier_note: Code and brain figures reproduced. The analyst listed three comparison targets and omitted observed industry money, which is the fourth. Paper claim reproduced.

summary_issues: Subgraph sizes: abstract (p.1 lines 10-11) says 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000; Methods (p.6 line 404) and Table 2 use 200, 500, 800, 1000. Verified.

CELF++ share: abstract (p.1 line 14) says 11.2 percent; body (p.8 line 478, p.13 line 949) says 12.9 percent. 122.95/954.90 = 12.9 percent. The summary should quote 12.9. mc_stability_check.py docstring repeats 11.2; the influence-modeling-reference skill calls it a share of true spread, but it is a share of IMM spread.
Abstract IMM 955.24 +/- 0.74 and RIS 951.27 +/- 2.22 do not match Table 2 (954.90 +/- 1.27 and 952.53 +/- 2.72). Verified.
PageRank share: 921.78/954.90 = 96.5 percent by arithmetic, but the abstract, discussion and conclusion say 96.3 percent. The summary is right to quote 96.5 from Table 2.
Runtime ratio: 323.5 s / 0.4 s = 809x; the paper says 794x (abstract line 19; discussion line 969). Verified.

CELF++ at 500 nodes: text line 565 says 4.56 and Table 2 says 4.91; CELF++ growth is +633 percent in text and +740 percent in Table 4. Table 2 value is consistent with the stated CV of 71.5 percent. Verified.
Growth percentages: text (lines 561-562) gives Degree +411 and PageRank +403; Table 4 gives +410 and +404. Verified.

Authors' causes: the summary says the authors blame only the MC budget and Python. The paper also names importance-based sampling bias (p.12 lines 929-939; p.14 lines 1074-1083), so 'only' is inaccurate.

Extrapolations: RIS 795 s at 10,000 nodes (p.13 line 978) is not linear from 64.9 s at 1000 nodes (about 649 s). CELF++ '840 s for 1000 nodes' (line 985) conflicts with its measured 688.4 s maximum at 1000 nodes (line 655). Both are unmeasured extrapolations.
PageRank 5 s at 10,000 nodes appears only in Limitations (line 1047), not in the Discussion. Verified.
Dangling centrality uses degree as the connectivity proxy (p.6 lines 389-390), so the tested method is not the published metric. Verified.
Minor share and ratio drift: PageRank gap 3.5 percent (line 494) vs 3.7 percent (line 975); RIS vs PageRank 3.3 percent (line 666) vs 3.2 percent by arithmetic (952.53 vs 921.78).
RIS theta = min(10000, 50n) equals 10,000 at every tested size (p.6 line 417), so RIS runs a fixed budget rather than a theory-set sample size.

References: refs 9-11 are off-topic (traffic anomaly detection, side-channel attacks, sample-size guidance) but cited for IM claims; ref 52 has no authors; ref 54 author field reads 'Others'; line 1117 refers to heuristics 'proposed in SATIC', an undefined term.

Analyst line cites wrong: top-45 pre-cut is budget_frontier.py line 137 (not 131); SEED keying is lines 80-82 (not 66-69); MEA-7 ledger is STATE.md 748-749 (not 765-768). Correct: mc_stability_check 3-19 and 4-5; salience_shock 44; optimize docstring 3-12; per_topic_coalition 114; kb_benchmark 29.

Unsourced Paul-position claims: the stated joint-optimizer position (GCOMB-style learned policies at scale), Paul saying more centrality research is needed, and a brain note 'RIS/IMM unneeded at 533 nodes' were not found in brain STATE, DECISIONS, CONSTRAINTS or DEADENDS, nor by a folder grep for GCOMB, RIS/IMM, forms of centrality. Remove or source before vault entry.
